source_text.body:
Fix a mobile web app by voice from a park bench
A developer used phone voice mode to give feedback to a coding agent, which started working up fixes to their mobile webapp while they were outdoors.
·
Nov 10, 2026
Done with a
custom-built or unnamed agent
What they did
While on a bench at Albany Bulb at sunset, the developer tried the latest revision of their mobile webapp on their phone. They then used the phone's voice mode to give feedback to their coding agent, which began working up fixes. The source doesn't name the agent or say how the fixes were reviewed.
How it went
The agent started on the fixes while the developer stayed outdoors, and they describe it as a revelation for working on the go. The source doesn't report whether the fixes worked.
Worth knowing
The setup needed only a phone with voice mode and cell service; the author mentions Starlink as a possible option but doesn't use it.
Try it yourself
with
Claude Code
Copy prompt
Open my mobile web app in [path to project folder] and I'll describe problems I see on my phone by voice. For each issue, find the cause, make the fix, and run the app's tests or a build to check it. When I'm done talking, give me a short list of what you changed and anything you weren't sure about. Don't push or deploy anything until I review the changes.
Original source: https://news.ycombinator.com/item?id=50444977
